Separating the two lets us ask whether a practice is punishment at all, and only then whether it is justified. If the definition already includes a justification, such as "deserved suffering," then debates about deterrence or rehabilitation become definitional disputes rather than moral ones, and practices can be called punishment that no one has yet shown to be defensible. This is why philosophers such as H.L.A. Hart treat the definition and the justification as separate questions.
